title: GitHub - ruairidhflint/news-blocklist: A DNS blocklist of news and current-affairs sites worldwide: a curated core plus news outlets from Wikidata. Hosts, domains, adblock, wildcard and dnsmasq formats.

content_html:
A DNS blocklist of news and current-affairs websites, for people who want a break from the news.

It covers newspapers, broadcasters' news sites, news agencies, news magazines, political news and commentary, business news, local news and news aggregators, worldwide. Major and regional outlets are curated in this repository. The long tail of smaller news sites is pulled from Wikidata, filtered automatically, checked against DNS, and refreshed every week.

Works with Pi-hole, AdGuard Home, uBlock Origin, AdGuard, dnsmasq, hosts files and any blocker that subscribes to a list by URL.

List Sites Hostnames (hosts format)
news 14,314 30,863
news-lite 6,762 15,936

Choose a list

List What's in it Use it when
news Everything: the curated outlets plus news sites listed on Wikidata. You want news gone, including local papers and niche outlets. Recommended.
news-lite The curated outlets plus the more popular news sites from Wikidata (domains in the Tranco top 200,000). You want the major and regional names blocked with a list half the size, or you're editing a hosts file by hand.

Both block the same major sites. news adds thousands of smaller ones.

Download

Each list comes in five formats. Use the URL as-is to subscribe; lists update when the data changes and at least weekly.

Format news news-lite
hosts hosts/news.txt hosts/news-lite.txt
domains domains/news.txt domains/news-lite.txt
wildcard wildcard/news.txt wildcard/news-lite.txt
adblock adblock/news.txt adblock/news-lite.txt
dnsmasq dnsmasq/news.txt dnsmasq/news-lite.txt
  • adblock, wildcard and dnsmasq entries block a domain and all its subdomains. Use one of these if your blocker supports it.
  • hosts and domains list exact hostnames, because a hosts file can't match subdomains. Each site is expanded to the names people actually visit (www., m., amp., edition. and so on) using DNS checks.

How to use it

Pi-hole · Lists (v6) or Adlists (v5) → add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ruairidhflint/news-blocklist/main/lists/adblock/news.txt → run Update Gravity. Pi-hole v6 (and v5 with FTL 5.22 or later) reads the adblock format and blocks subdomains; on older versions use lists/domains/news.txt.

AdGuard Home · Filters → DNS blocklists → Add blocklist → Add a custom list → paste the adblock/news.txt URL.

uBlock Origin · Dashboard → Filter lists → Import (at the bottom) → paste the adblock/news.txt URL → Apply changes. Blocked pages show uBlock's warning page.

AdGuard (browser extension and apps) · Filters → Custom → Add custom filter → paste the adblock/news.txt URL.

dnsmasq / OpenWrt · download lists/dnsmasq/news.txt into /etc/dnsmasq.d/ (or add it as a conf-file) and restart dnsmasq.

Hosts file (macOS, Linux, Windows) · append lists/hosts/news-lite.txt (or news.txt) to /etc/hosts (C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts on Windows). Turn off your browser's "secure DNS" / DNS-over-HTTPS, or it will skip the hosts file.

What counts as news

Blocked: general news (national, regional and local), politics, world affairs, business and economic news, opinion and commentary on current affairs, news agencies, broadcasters' news sites and 24-hour news channels, news and current-affairs magazines, tabloids, fact-checkers, news aggregators and the news sections of web portals.

Not blocked: sport-only, entertainment and celebrity, technology, gaming and science publications, lifestyle magazines, trade press, academic journals, government sites, and TV or radio streaming services (unless they're the same site as the news).

The curated lists follow this line. The part pulled from Wikidata is filtered to follow it, but the filters rely on Wikidata's own descriptions and miss some sites (see Limitations). The line isn't always sharp either. If you think a site is on the wrong side of it, open an issue.

Sites that do more than news

DNS blocking works on whole hostnames. It can't block example.com/news and leave example.com/weather working. When news is the main thing a host serves, it's blocked anyway, and anything else on that host goes with it. Where a company runs other services on separate hostnames (email, logins, streaming apps), only the news hostnames are listed.

Limitations

  • News inside other apps and sites isn't blocked: social media feeds, search results ("Top stories"), YouTube, podcasts, and phone news widgets that use shared platform APIs. Pair this list with a social-media list if those are a problem.
  • Browsers with DNS-over-HTTPS bypass hosts files and local DNS blockers. Turn it off or point it at your blocker.
  • The Wikidata part is filtered, not reviewed. It adds about 10,000 smaller sites automatically. Outlets that Wikidata classes as gaming, sports or trade publications are dropped, and anything whose description, genre or hostname suggests a specialist outlet goes to a review queue instead of the list. Many Wikidata entries have no description, so some specialist, defunct or off-topic sites still get through. Popular domains are never added automatically. If something's wrong, report it.
  • The curated core was compiled with an AI model, not by a person working site by site. See How it's built. Expect some mistakes at this scale.

How it's built

data/curated/*.txt     curated outlets, by region                 ─┐
data/generated/        news outlets from Wikidata, DNS results    ─┼─► scripts/build.py ─► lists/
data/allow.txt         domains never blocked                      ─┘

  1. Curated outlets (data/curated/) are the core: major and regional news sites in every region, plus aggregators. The first version was compiled with an AI model (Claude). It went through the most popular domains that Wikidata lists as news outlets one by one, then added outlets Wikidata was missing from its own knowledge. Every hostname resolves in DNS (checked weekly), and most additions were checked against the site's live homepage. Entries are hostnames; a comment starting mixed: documents what else blocking that host breaks.

  2. Wikidata supplies the long tail. scripts/refresh.py asks for everything that is a newspaper, news website, news agency, news magazine or news channel (the classes are in data/wikidata-classes.txt) and still has an official website. It then drops:

    • defunct outlets and old website addresses;
    • outlets Wikidata also classes as something out of scope: video game, sports and trade publications, academic journals, shops, databases and the like;
    • outlets whose Wikidata genre or main subject is sport, music, film, technology, science, fashion or similar;
    • government, military and education domains;
    • websites that are just a page on a shared host;
    • domains in data/allow.txt.

    Sites whose Wikidata description, genre or hostname only suggests a specialist outlet (gaming, tech, trade press, weather, crypto …) aren't added either. They go to data/generated/review.txt, because the same words turn up in real newspapers too (the Weatherford Democrat, the Daily Gamecock).

  3. A popularity guard. A site on a domain in the Tranco top 25,000 is never added automatically, so a bad Wikidata edit can't block a major site. Those go to the review queue too. Each queued site waits for a person to add it to a curated file or to allow.txt.

  4. DNS checks remove dead sites and find the subdomains each site uses, for the hosts-format lists.

  5. Tests check every build. A reference set of major news sites must be blocked in every list and format, and sites that aren't news (Google, the NHS, Sky Sports, Yahoo Mail and others) must not be. A build that fails isn't published.

  6. GitHub Actions rebuilds the lists on every change and refreshes from Wikidata every Monday. A refresh that would shrink the list sharply is refused, so a Wikidata outage can't empty it.

Run it yourself with Python 3.10+ and no dependencies:

python3 scripts/refresh.py   # needs network: Wikidata, DNS, Tranco, Public Suffix List
python3 scripts/build.py     # offline: writes lists/ and the stats above
python3 scripts/test_lists.py

Contributing

Missing a site, or a site blocked by mistake? Open an issue or see CONTRIBUTING.md: most changes are one line in data/curated/ or data/allow.txt.

Credits and license

The list and scripts are MIT licensed.

  • Outlet data from Wikidata, available under CC0.
  • Site popularity from the Tranco list (Le Pochat et al., NDSS 2019), used only to decide what needs review.
  • Domain parsing with the Public Suffix List (MPL 2.0), downloaded at build time.

Wikidata supplies the long tail. scripts/refresh.py asks for everything that is a newspaper, news website, news agency, news magazine or news channel (the classes are in data/wikidata-classes.txt) and still has an official website. It then drops: defunct outlets and old website addresses; outlets Wikidata also classes as something out of scope: video game, sports and trade publications, academic journals, shops, databases and the like; outlets whose Wikidata genre or main subject is sport, music, film, technology, science, fashion or similar; government, military and education domains; websites that are just a page on a shared host; domains in data/allow.txt. Sites whose Wikidata description, genre or hostname only suggests a specialist outlet (gaming, tech, trade press, weather, crypto …) aren't added either. They go to data/generated/review.txt, because the same words turn up in real newspapers too (the Weatherford Democrat, the Daily Gamecock). A popularity guard. A site on a domain in the Tranco top 25,000 is never added automatically, so a bad Wikidata edit can't block a major site. Those go to the review queue too. Each queued site waits for a person to add it to a curated file or to allow.txt. DNS checks remove dead sites and find the subdomains each site uses, for the hosts-format lists. Tests check every build. A reference set of major news sites must be blocked in every list and format, and sites that aren't news (Google, the NHS, Sky Sports, Yahoo Mail and others) must not be. A build that fails isn't published. GitHub Actions rebuilds the lists on every change and refreshes from Wikidata every Monday. A refresh that would shrink the list sharply is refused, so a Wikidata outage can't empty it. Run it yourself with Python 3.10+ and no dependencies: python3 scripts/refresh.py # needs network: Wikidata, DNS, Tranco, Public Suffix List python3 scripts/build.py # offline: writes lists/ and the stats above python3 scripts/test_lists.py Contributing Missing a site, or a site blocked by mistake? Open an issue or see CONTRIBUTING.md: most changes are one line in data/curated/ or data/allow.txt. Credits and license The list and scripts are MIT licensed. Outlet data from Wikidata, available under CC0. Site popularity from the Tranco list (Le Pochat et al., NDSS 2019), used only to decide what needs review. Domain parsing with the Public Suffix List (MPL 2.0), downloaded at build time.

content_html_zh:
A DNS blocklist of news and current-affairs websites, for people who want a break from the news.

It covers newspapers, broadcasters' news sites, news agencies, news magazines, political news and commentary, business news, local news and news aggregators, worldwide. Major and regional outlets are curated in this repository. The long tail of smaller news sites is pulled from Wikidata, filtered automatically, checked against DNS, and refreshed every week.

Works with Pi-hole, AdGuard Home, uBlock Origin, AdGuard, dnsmasq, hosts files and any blocker that subscribes to a list by URL.

List Sites Hostnames (hosts format)
news 14,314 30,863
news-lite 6,762 15,936

Choose a list

List 里面有什么 Use it when
news Everything: the curated outlets plus news sites listed on Wikidata. You want news gone, including local papers and niche outlets. 受到推崇的。
news-lite The curated outlets plus the more popular news sites from Wikidata (domains in the Tranco top 200,000). You want the major and regional names blocked with a list half the size, or you're editing a hosts file by hand.

Both block the same major sites. news adds thousands of smaller ones.

下载

Each list comes in five formats. Use the URL as-is to subscribe; lists update when the data changes and at least weekly.

格式 news news-lite
hosts hosts/news.txt hosts/news-lite.txt
域 domains/news.txt domains/news-lite.txt
wildcard wildcard/news.txt wildcard/news-lite.txt
adblock adblock/news.txt adblock/news-lite.txt
dnsmasq dnsmasq/news.txt dnsmasq/news-lite.txt
  • adblock, wildcard and dnsmasq entries block a domain and all its subdomains. Use one of these if your blocker supports it.
  • hosts and domains list exact hostnames, because a hosts file can't match subdomains. Each site is expanded to the names people actually visit (www., m., amp., edition. and so on) using DNS checks.

如何使用

Pi-hole · Lists (v6) or Adlists (v5) → add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ruairidhflint/news-blocklist/main/lists/adblock/news.txt → run Update Gravity. Pi-hole v6 (and v5 with FTL 5.22 or later) reads the adblock format and blocks subdomains; on older versions use lists/domains/news.txt.

AdGuard Home · Filters → DNS blocklists → Add blocklist → Add a custom list → paste the adblock/news.txt URL.

uBlock Origin · Dashboard → Filter lists → Import (at the bottom) → paste the adblock/news.txt URL → Apply changes. Blocked pages show uBlock's warning page.

What counts as news

Blocked: general news (national, regional and local), politics, world affairs, business and economic news, opinion and commentary on current affairs, news agencies, broadcasters' news sites and 24-hour news channels, news and current-affairs magazines, tabloids, fact-checkers, news aggregators and the news sections of web portals.

Not blocked: sport-only, entertainment and celebrity, technology, gaming and science publications, lifestyle magazines, trade press, academic journals, government sites, and TV or radio streaming services (unless they're the same site as the news).

The curated lists follow this line. The part pulled from Wikidata is filtered to follow it, but the filters rely on Wikidata's own descriptions and miss some sites (see Limitations). The line isn't always sharp either. If you think a site is on the wrong side of it, open an issue.

Sites that do more than news

DNS blocking works on whole hostnames. It can't block example.com/news and leave example.com/weather working. When news is the main thing a host serves, it's blocked anyway, and anything else on that host goes with it. Where a company runs other services on separate hostnames (email, logins, streaming apps), only the news hostnames are listed.

局限性

  • News inside other apps and sites isn't blocked: social media feeds, search results ("Top stories"), YouTube, podcasts, and phone news widgets that use shared platform APIs. Pair this list with a social-media list if those are a problem.
  • Browsers with DNS-over-HTTPS bypass hosts files and local DNS blockers. Turn it off or point it at your blocker.
  • The Wikidata part is filtered, not reviewed. It adds about 10,000 smaller sites automatically. Outlets that Wikidata classes as gaming, sports or trade publications are dropped, and anything whose description, genre or hostname suggests a specialist outlet goes to a review queue instead of the list. Many Wikidata entries have no description, so some specialist, defunct or off-topic sites still get through. Popular domains are never added automatically. If something's wrong, report it.
  • The curated core was compiled with an AI model, not by a person working site by site. See How it's built. Expect some mistakes at this scale.

它是如何构建的

data/curated/*.txt     curated outlets, by region                 ─┐
data/generated/        news outlets from Wikidata, DNS results    ─┼─► scripts/build.py ─► lists/
data/allow.txt         domains never blocked                      ─┘
  1. Curated outlets (data/curated/) are the core: major and regional news sites in every region, plus aggregators. The first version was compiled with an AI model (Claude). It went through the most popular domains that Wikidata lists as news outlets one by one, then added outlets Wikidata was missing from its own knowledge. Every hostname resolves in DNS (checked weekly), and most additions were checked against the site's live homepage. Entries are hostnames; a comment starting mixed: documents what else blocking that host breaks.
  2. Wikidata supplies the long tail. scripts/refresh.py asks for everything that is a newspaper, news website, news agency, news magazine or news channel (the classes are in data/wikidata-classes.txt) and still has an official website. It then drops: defunct outlets and old website addresses; outlets Wikidata also classes as something out of scope: video game, sports and trade publications, academic journals, shops, databases and the like; outlets whose Wikidata genre or main subject is sport, music, film, technology, science, fashion or similar; government, military and education domains; websites that are just a page on a shared host; domains in data/allow.txt. Sites whose Wikidata description, genre or hostname only suggests a specialist outlet (gaming, tech, trade press, weather, crypto …) aren't added either. They go to data/generated/review.txt, because the same words turn up in real newspapers too (the Weatherford Democrat, the Daily Gamecock).
  3. A popularity guard. A site on a domain in the Tranco top 25,000 is never added automatically, so a bad Wikidata edit can't block a major site. Those go to the review queue too. Each queued site waits for a person to add it to a curated file or to allow.txt.
  4. DNS checks remove dead sites and find the subdomains each site uses, for the hosts-format lists.
  5. Tests check every build. A reference set of major news sites must be blocked in every list and format, and sites that aren't news (Google, the NHS, Sky Sports, Yahoo Mail and others) must not be. A build that fails isn't published.
  6. GitHub Actions rebuilds the lists on every change and refreshes from Wikidata every Monday. A refresh that would shrink the list sharply is refused, so a Wikidata outage can't empty it.

Run it yourself with Python 3.10+ and no dependencies:

python3 scripts/refresh.py   # needs network: Wikidata, DNS, Tranco, Public Suffix List
python3 scripts/build.py     # offline: writes lists/ and the stats above
python3 scripts/test_lists.py
